title: Content Provenance, Access and Attribution
description: 59 cards for the organizations, working groups, specifications and proposals that decide where content came from (provenance), what may be done with it (access, licensing, payment) and whether its source gets credited (attribution), and where the Model Context Protocol fits among them.
note: One person's working notes. Status lines carry the dates the sources gave, so check upstream before relying on one.

layers.provenance: where content came from and what was done to it, carried as signed records
layers.access: whether a crawler or agent may read or use content, and how that preference is expressed
layers.licensing: the terms and prices for use, in a form machines can read
layers.attribution: whether the source is named and credited where the content ends up
layers.payments: how a use gets paid for, from HTTP 402 to agent checkout
layers.identity: who the agent, crawler or signer is
layers.governance: the foundations, policy bodies and regulation around the rest

stages.at-rest: content or a skill is signed where it is stored
stages.in-transit: the credential travels with the content across a tool call
stages.boundary: a gateway or hook checks it on the way through
stages.after-delivery: credit and reporting once the content has left the protocol and its metadata is gone
stages.trust: who may sign or report, and how that is decided. Not a place on the path, but every other stage depends on it

sections.title: Topics

sections.title: Topics

sections.title: Topics

sections.title: Related

cards.name: AAIF Observability and Traceability WG
cards.status: Nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model plan; provenance initiative lead named 2026-09-02; OTel cross-domain provenance proposal 2026-10-28
cards.summary: Working group on agent-level observability, above the OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry conventions.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Evidence records**: tamper-evident records of agent behavior ([Evidence Record Spec proposal](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/issues/37)).

- **Liaisons**: the [liaison roster](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/issues/11) has no content-side member, so nothing connects the group to [[content-telemetry]].

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - The conventions it builds above, and what they leave out: [[otel-mcp]].

cards.name: AAIF Security and Privacy WG

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:

- **Agent trust manifests**: from [[project-nanda]].

cards.name: Agent Identity and Manifest Standard
cards.status: v0.1 draft
cards.summary: DID-based agent identity, proof of what content the agent is licensed to access, and a link from identity to the telemetry endpoint.

sections.title: Topics

sections.title: Related

cards.name: Agent Payments Protocol

cards.summary: Mandates that prove a human authorized an agent purchase.

sections.title: Topics

cards.name: Agent Skills
cards.status: Joined AAIF 2026-10-22
cards.summary: The SKILL.md format for packaging instructions and files for agents.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Skill provenance**: signing, lineage and authorship of skills ([[agent-skills-signing]]).
- **Skill rights and payment**: paying authors and respecting licenses ([[skills-marketplace]]).

cards.name: Agent Skills at-rest signing threads
cards.status: Six open discussions in Ideas, one maintainer, no convergence
cards.summary: Proposals for signing, lockfiles and lineage of SKILL.md folders: signature in frontmatter ([#252](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/discussions/252)), SKILL.sig sidecar ([#393](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/discussions/393)), skills-lock.json ([#588](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/discussions/588)), `metadata.source` ([#564](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/discussions/564)), `metadata.derived-from` ([#620](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/discussions/620)), skill-evidence documents keyed by digest ([#643](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/discussions/643)).

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Copy sprawl**: tracking copies, which outnumber originals. One dataset has half of SKILL.md files as verbatim copies, and only 11.1% of fixes reach every copy.
- **Field ownership**: separating identity (digest), lineage (source, derived-from), authorship (signature) and evidence (keyed by digest) so each thread owns one field.
- **Retraction and signer identity**: withdrawing a bad skill and naming who signed it ([[cawg]]). No thread covers either.

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - Digests from [[mcp-skills-extension]], catalog-side signing in [[ai-catalog]], sidecars from [[c2pa]], verification tiers in [[aaif-security-privacy-wg]].

cards.name: Agentic AI Foundation

sections.title: Topics

sections.title: Topics

cards.name: AI Disclosures Project
cards.status: Convenings at Bellagio (April 2026), Foo Camp (June 2026), MSR NYC (September 2026)
cards.summary: Project housed at Code for Science and Society working on the standards and mechanisms for value distribution in the human and AI economy. Prototypes include [[skills-marketplace]], the Open Memory Protocol Consortium and the Open Alpha Registry.

cards.name: ai.robots.txt

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Crawler blocking today**: giving site operators ready-made blocks, and a record of what they deploy compared with what [[ietf-aipref]] specifies.

cards.name: C2PA
aliases: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
cards.status: Spec 2.5 published October 2026
cards.summary: Standards body for content credentials: signed manifests (claims and assertions) bound to an asset, with ingredients for derived works. Reference code is maintained by the [[content-authenticity-initiative]].

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Asset provenance**: proving where an asset came from and what was done to it, with the record cryptographically bound to the asset.
- **Text and JSON provenance**: binding a credential to formats with no metadata slot. 2.5 added Appendix A.9.3 guidance for JSON, which [[mcp-c2pa-in-meta]] relies on. The conformance text rubric has no JSON group yet.
- **Stripped metadata**: recovering provenance after the manifest is removed, through watermarks and fingerprints on the soft-binding algorithm list (60 entries by 2026-10-28).
- **Signer trust**: deciding who may sign, through a trust list and a conformance program.

sections.title: Related
sections.text:
- Identity and consent assertions come from [[cawg]].
- Signing skill folders: [[agent-skills-signing]].
- Its trust layer is compared with [[aaif-identity-trust-wg]] and [[spur-coalition]].

cards.name: C2PA content credentials in MCP _meta
cards.status: Discussion closed 2026-09-25 with all spec-repo discussions; no SEP filed yet
cards.summary: Carry a [[c2pa]] credential for tool results and resources in MCP `_meta` under `org.c2pa/credential`.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Provenance in transit**: keeping a credential attached as content crosses from server to client.
- **A venue**: finding an owner, since no WG or IG covers content provenance and [PR 3336](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/3336) requires a WG or IG thread before a SEP PR.
- **Track choice**: deciding between an `experimental-ext-` repo under SEP-3392 and a Standards Track SEP.
- **Where the field lives**: choosing between a top-level field and `_meta`, the same question [[mcp-sep-3094-citations]] faces.

sections.title: Related
sections.text:
- A credential check could run as an interceptor validator ([[mcp-interceptors]]).
- Lineage key overlap: [[openlineage]].

cards.name: CC Signals
cards.status: GitHub draft unchanged since 2025-12; v2 to make attribution a requirement
cards.summary: Preference signals for AI reuse with terms attached: Credit, Credit + Direct Contribution, Credit + Ecosystem Contribution, Credit + Open. Layered on [[ietf-aipref]] vocabulary.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Reuse with reciprocity**: letting stewards allow AI reuse with terms attached, for those who do not want a plain opt-out.
- **Checking credit**: knowing whether credit was given, which links to [[content-telemetry]] and [[mcp-sep-3094-citations]].

cards.name: Cloudflare Content Signals
cards.status: Individual AIPREF draft; parsed by policycheck
cards.summary: Three robots.txt categories, `search`, `ai-input` and `ai-train`, proposed as [[ietf-aipref]] vocabulary.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Use categories**: separating search indexing, use as model input and training in one signal.

cards.name: Content Authenticity Initiative
cards.status: Maintains c2pa-rs, c2pa-python, c2pa-js and c2patool
cards.summary: Adobe-led initiative that maintains the open-source reference implementations of [[c2pa]].

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Reference SDKs**: giving developers one implementation for signing and verifying manifests, with a Rust core and Python and JS bindings.
- **Text handlers**: signing plain and structured text in practice. Structured-text and plain-text A.8 handlers merged in c2pa-rs behind an experimental flag (2026-09); HTML, XML and TTML handlers are open.

cards.name: Content Telemetry
cards.status: v1.0 published 2026-09-02; signed events deferred (section 8.9)
cards.summary: Five reportable stages: `content_retrieved`, `content_grounded`, `content_cited`, `content_presented`, `content_engaged`. Manifest discovery at `/.well-known/content-telemetry.json`. `license_ref` joins it to the licensing layer ([[rsl]], [[iab-comp]]).

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Usage reporting**: reporting how AI systems use content after retrieval, in five events.
- **Demanding conformance**: a manifest cannot require a conformance level from an agent (section 8.5).
- **MCP binding**: emitting `content_cited` and `content_presented` from MCP clients, the events [[mcp-sep-3094-citations]] `citations.render` would need. telemetry-js ships an `MCPSessionTracker`.

sections.title: Related
sections.text:
- Execution traces, which stop at the tool call: [[otel-mcp]].
- [[counter]] plans to reference it in phase two.

sections.title: Topics

sections.title: Topics

cards.name: IETF AI Preferences Working Group
cards.status: vocab-08 (2026-09-13) without consensus; attach-05 (2026-08-18); IETF 127 sessions 2026-11-16 and 11-19
cards.summary: Vocabulary for AI usage preferences and how they attach to content (`Content-Usage` header and robots.txt directive).

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Shared vocabulary**: defining training and other AI uses so every crawler reads a preference the same way.
- **Attachment**: binding a preference to content through a `Content-Usage` header and robots.txt directive.
- **Downstream survival**: keeping preferences intact through model redistribution, caching and embeddings ([issues 245](https://github.com/ietf-wg-aipref/drafts/issues/245) and [246](https://github.com/ietf-wg-aipref/drafts/issues/246)).
- **Inference-time use**: covering grounding and agent use, which the vocabulary does not yet do. [[microsoft-grounding-preference]] is the first vendor signal there. MCP has no field for a server to declare it.

sections.title: Related
sections.text:
- Individual drafts: [[aipref-training-token]], [[cloudflare-content-signals]], and the [[creative-commons]] exclusions and parameters drafts.
- Enforcement side: [[ietf-web-bot-auth]]. Layered on by [[cc-signals]].

cards.name: Model Context Protocol
cards.status: Next spec release moved to 2027-03-30 (SEP-3398); WG-first rule for SEPs
cards.summary: The protocol between agents and the tools, resources, prompts and skills they read. MCP is the hop where content provenance can be carried or lost.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Content provenance ownership**: no WG or IG owns content provenance or attribution.
- **Usage declarations**: no field lets a server declare how its content may be used for training or grounding ([[ietf-aipref]]).
- **Credit reporting**: nothing reports display or credit past the last hop ([[content-telemetry]]).

sections.title: Related

- Threads: [[mcp-c2pa-in-meta]], [[mcp-sep-3094-citations]], [[mcp-skills-extension]], [[mcp-interceptors]].

cards.name: OpenTelemetry for MCP
cards.status: Conventions in Development; built into the Python SDK since v2.0.0; merged for the TypeScript SDK 2026-10-31, not yet released
cards.summary: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for MCP spans and metrics, and the SDKs that emit them. Spans are named `{mcp.method.name} {target}`, for example `tools/call get-weather`, with `mcp.session.id`, `mcp.protocol.version` and `jsonrpc.request.id`. Trace context travels in `params._meta` under three keys that [SEP-414](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/414-request-meta) proposed in April 2025 and the [2026-07-28 spec reserves](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#_meta): `traceparent`, `tracestate` and `baggage`.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Metadata that already travels with a tool call**: a trace id is the one piece of metadata MCP carries end to end today, client to server and back, in the same `_meta` slot that [[mcp-c2pa-in-meta]] proposes for content credentials. The propagation rules are a precedent for any other credential that has to survive the hop.
- **What a span does not say**: the conventions make tool arguments and results opt-in attributes marked as sensitive (`gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`, `gen_ai.tool.call.result`), so a trace shows which tool ran, when and for how long, and nothing about the content that came back or where it came from. That gap is where [[content-telemetry]] and the [[aaif-observability-traceability-wg]] sit.
- **SDK coverage**: the Python SDK has emitted client and server spans since v2.0.0 ([#2381](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/2381), 2026-03-31, middleware form in [#2941](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/2941)), with no metrics. The TypeScript SDK adds spans and `mcp.client.operation.duration` and `mcp.server.operation.duration` histograms, on by default once an OpenTelemetry SDK is registered ([#3115](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3115), merged 2026-10-31, not in a release as of 2026-11-08). The C# SDK has an `Experimental.ModelContextProtocol` activity source. The Go and Java SDKs have no built-in instrumentation.

sections.title: Related
sections.text:
- [SEP-2028](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2028), open, would forward `_meta` entries to HTTP headers for distributed tracing. [SEP-2448](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2448), server execution telemetry, closed without merging in March 2026.
- Lineage after the tool call, rather than the call itself: [[openlineage]].

cards.name: Project NANDA
cards.summary: MIT-originated agent registry and trust-manifest work, discussed in [[aaif-security-privacy-wg]].

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Agent trust manifests**: trust metadata for agents in an open registry.

cards.name: Really Simple Licensing
cards.status: RSL 1.0 published 2025-12-10
cards.summary: XML vocabulary for usage and compensation terms (per-crawl, per-inference, subscription, attribution-only), discovered from robots.txt, RSS, HTTP headers or HTML. Includes a Crawler Authorization Protocol and an Open License Protocol on OAuth 2.0. The RSL Collective is the collecting society behind it.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Machine-readable terms**: publishing usage terms and prices that crawlers and AI systems can read and accept.
- **Adoption**: getting model developers to honor it on the open web. None has committed; [[microsoft-publisher-content-marketplace]] is reported to support it.
- **Enforcement**: supplying the lever [[content-telemetry]] manifests lack, through a SPUR profile binding drafted for the RSL WG.

cards.name: SEP-2640 Skills Extension
cards.status: Final 2026-09-13; Beta under SEP-3392
cards.summary: Serves [[agent-skills]] over MCP, with digests and a `_meta` hook for intermediaries.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Skills over MCP**: distributing skills to clients with digests and a `_meta` hook for intermediaries.

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - At-rest signing is not on the Skills WG agenda ([[agent-skills-signing]]).

cards.name: SEP-3094 Granular Citations
cards.status: Open, no sponsor; revised 2026-09-04; an implementation PR open from Perplexity; dormancy clock to about 2027-01-15
cards.summary: Citations on tool results bound by CommonMark links in the text, each a flat schema.org CreativeWork, granularity via URL fragments, integrity deferred. A `citations.render` client capability.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Citations in transit**: keeping sources attached from tool result to the answer a user sees.
- **Sponsorship and venue**: finding a sponsor and a WG or IG discussion.
- **Field placement**: choosing a top-level field or `_meta` processed by [[mcp-interceptors]].
- **Reporting**: mapping to [[okfn]] `sources` and [[content-telemetry]] events.

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - Reviewers include [[okfn]] and [[wikimedia]] contributors.

cards.name: Shared AI training robots.txt token
cards.status: Individual draft posted 2026-10-30; Google, OpenAI, Microsoft and Anthropic committed to honor it
cards.summary: A robots.txt group whose `User-Agent` is the cross-vendor token `__usage_ai-training`, using ordinary `Allow` and `Disallow` rules. No new syntax. "AI Training" takes its definition from the [[ietf-aipref]] vocab draft.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **One training opt-out**: a single signal every major crawler operator honors, with no new robots.txt grammar.
- **Compliance**: getting honored signals to change outputs. Prompting can still surface disallowed content.

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - An alternative to the attach draft's `Content-Usage` directive in [[ietf-aipref]].

cards.name: Skills Marketplace
cards.status: Initial testing with O'Reilly authors
cards.summary: Monetizable, rights-protected, interoperable skills, with skillproof benchmarks.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Paying skill authors**: choosing a payout basis for skills, measured contribution or invocation count.
- **Multi-source skills**: crediting every source behind a skill ([[openattribution]], [[c2pa]]).
- **Missing metadata**: no skill registry frontmatter carries author, license or source ([[agent-skills-signing]]).

cards.name: Spawning
cards.status: datadiligence dormant since 2024-10
cards.summary: Maker of datadiligence, a Python library that checks works against known opt-out methods inside a training pipeline.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Pipeline-side compliance**: checking works against known opt-outs inside a training pipeline. No other open-source implementation of this step appears on these cards.

cards.name: SPUR Coalition
cards.status: Content Telemetry v1.0 published 2026-09-02
cards.summary: Publisher coalition founded by the BBC, FT, Guardian, Sky News and Telegraph, with the AP as first US member. Stewards [[content-telemetry]] and the publisher accreditation profile and conformance mark. Sister body [[openattribution]] maintains SDKs and profiles.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Visibility past retrieval**: letting publishers see grounding, citation, display and engagement, not only the fetch.
- **Verifying reports**: checking self-reported events through sampled audits or canary content. Signed events are deferred to a later version of the spec (section 8.9).
- **Publisher accreditation**: a conformance mark for agents that report at the required level.

cards.name: Universal Commerce Protocol
cards.status: Google-led consortium, no foundation home
cards.summary: Merchant commerce protocol. [[openattribution]] has an `org.openattribution.telemetry` vendor extension for it.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Cross-merchant commerce**: agent commerce across merchants, compared with [[acp]] in [[aaif-agentic-commerce-wg]].

cards.name: W3C
cards.summary: Web standards body. Hosts [[w3c-odrl]] and [[w3c-tdmrep]], and the DID and Verifiable Credentials specs [[aims]] uses.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **Web vocabularies**: rights and identity standards for the web.

cards.name: W3C ODRL
cards.status: 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation; a W3C WG for 3.0 is being chartered; ai-vocab draft
cards.summary: Policy language for permissions, prohibitions and duties on content.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Policy language**: one model for permissions, prohibitions and duties that [[rsl]], IPTC RightsML ([[iptc]]), [[cawg]] and [[w3c-tdmrep]] all point at.
- **AI actions**: adding AI-specific actions to the vocabulary (the `ai-vocab` draft).

cards.name: W3C TDM Reservation Protocol Community Group
cards.status: CG draft; last push 2026-09
cards.summary: The EU DSM Article 4 text and data mining opt-out: `tdm-reservation` and `tdm-policy` by HTTP header, HTML meta or `/.well-known/tdmrep.json`.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text: - **EU TDM opt-out**: a machine-readable text and data mining reservation that satisfies EU DSM Article 4.

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - Being weighed for the EU recognized opt-out list ([[eu-ai-act-gpai-code]]). Points at [[w3c-odrl]] for detailed policy.

cards.name: Wikimedia
cards.status: Published investigation of OpenAI-run agents 2026-10-05; Wikipedians reviewing SEP-3094
cards.summary: Movement behind Wikipedia and Wikidata. Wikimedia Enterprise supplies Microsoft, Mistral and Perplexity, and volunteer contributors review citation and agent-identity proposals.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Identifiable agents**: knowing which agents are reading the projects ([[ietf-web-bot-auth]], [[aims]]).
- **Attribution for reuse**: meeting attribution requirements in agent answers. A WikiCite contributor listed six functions of citation on [[mcp-sep-3094-citations]], including provenance chains to primary sources.
- **A seat at the table**: [[open-future]] argued in December 2025 that Wikimedia needs one at [[aaif]].

cards.name: x402
cards.status: x402 Foundation (Linux Foundation) operational 2026-07-14; v2 spec
cards.summary: HTTP 402 payments in headers, with schemes `exact`, `upto`, `auth-capture` and `batch-settlement` and transports for HTTP, MCP and A2A. Successor in spirit to L402 (Lightning). Sibling of [[aaif]] under the Linux Foundation, not part of it.

sections.title: Topics
sections.text:
- **Machine payment**: paying for a request without accounts or API keys, the rail a licensing term ([[rsl]], [[iab-comp]]) would settle on.
- **Delegated spending**: authorization for agents spending on someone's behalf, which lives elsewhere ([[ap2]]).

sections.title: Related
sections.text: - Compared with other commerce specs in [[aaif-agentic-commerce-wg]].
